paragraphs: (A Tanna of a baraita.) He is mentioned in [Tosefta Chullin, beginning of chapter 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Chullin.8.1): “Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says: Fowl goes up with cheese on the table. Apikolos says: It is not eaten. Others say: Fowl is eaten.” Hyman considers it clear from this that it is a Tanna’s name. But in [Chullin 104b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.104b.11-12): “Agra, father-in-law of Rabbi Abba, taught: Fowl and cheese are eaten be-apikoren (casually, without being careful with them — [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Chullin.104b.11.1)). He taught it and he said it: without washing the hands and without wiping the mouth.” Likewise further on they said: “But Agra taught: Fowl and cheese are eaten be-apikorin, and some say be-apkolis,” and it is explained there to mean a cloth. Hyman infers that they did not have his Tosefta’s reading before them and considers their reading undoubtedly correct.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Hebrew of the linked Tosefta has אפיקולוס אומר. The accompanying English takes afikolos adverbially, “without any restriction,” and continues the preceding rabbi’s statement. Hyman instead takes Apikolos to be a Tanna’s name.

In the linked Bavli, Agra teaches that fowl and cheese may be eaten be-apikoren, which Rashi explains as without taking special care. The linked continuation repeats apikoren. The alternate form apkolis and its explanation as a cloth are reported by Hyman. He considers the Bavli’s reading undoubtedly correct and infers that its transmitters had a different Tosefta text.
